{{nihongo|'''Oiso Shrine'''|奥石神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

It is enshrined within Oisonomori (老蘇森), a nationally designated {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}}, along the {{ill|Nakasendō|Q1154479|qid=Q1154479}} (also called the Nakasendō), north of the Higashi-Oiso settlement.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The currently enshrined deity is the following single kami<ref name="説明板">Explanation board within the precincts.</ref>.
* {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}
The various deities enshrined in the main hall are hearth-fire prevention deities. Because the character for “kama” (sickle) was applied to “kamado” (hearth), the shrine came to be called “Kama Daimyōjin” or “Kama-no-miya.” Even today, parishioners maintain the custom of offering sickles to the shrine{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
According to the *Oiso Shrine Honki* (colophon dated September of the first year of {{ill|Shitoku|Q1146202|qid=Q1146202|lt=Shitoku}} ({{ill|1384|Q6347|qid=Q6347}})), the shrine began in the 5th year of the 7th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Kōrei|ar|الإمبراطور كوريه|arz|الامبراطور كوريه|azb|کوریه (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Kōrei|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆرێی|cs|Kórei|de|Kōrei|es|Kōrei Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوریه|fi|Kōrei|fr|Kōrei|he|קוריי, קיסר יפן|hr|Kōrei|id|Kaisar Kōrei|it|Kōrei|ja|孝霊天皇|ka|კორეი|ko|고레이 천황|nl|Korei|pl|Kōrei|pt|Korei|ro|Împăratul Kōrei|ru|Император Корэй|sh|Car Kōrei|simple|Emperor Kōrei|sl|Cesar Korej|sr|Кореи|sv|Korei|th|จักรพรรดิโคเร|tl|Emperador Korei|tr|Kōrei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Корей|uz|Imperator Kōrei|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōrei|zh|孝靈天皇|zh_classical|孝靈天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôrei Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝靈天皇|qid=Q313041}}, when Ishibe no Ōmuraji built a sacred altar in Oisonomori and enshrined the child deity of Ōtoshi-no-Kami{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}. It further states that during the reign of the 10th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kibitsuhiko}} established a palace and enshrined Okutsuhiko-no-Mikoto and Okutsuhime-no-Mikoto, and that during the reign of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}}, Kasa no Ason (a descendant of Kibitsuhiko) additionally enshrined {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} and {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|Q11487396|qid=Q11487396|lt=Tachibana-hime}}{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.

One theory holds that the shrine originated in primitive mountain worship with Mount Kinugasa as the {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}} (sacred mountain), and that the present site is a village shrine from which the {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}} at the mountain summit is worshiped from afar{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.

=== Overview ===
In the *{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}* record dated the first year of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), one household from Ōmi Province was assigned as {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711}} to the then “Oiso Deity”{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}. The *Oiso Shrine Honki* also records that in the first year of {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} ({{ill|851|Q29966|qid=Q29966}}), the shrine was granted the divine rank of Senior Sixth Rank Upper{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} In the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was known by names such as “Kama Daimyōjin” and “Kama-no-miya Shrine”{{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, it was designated a village shrine in October {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 9){{Sfn|Oiso Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}. It was promoted to a township shrine in February {{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}} (Meiji 14), designated a shrine receiving state offerings in April {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} (Meiji 41), and in February {{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}} ({{ill|Taishō era|ar|فترة تايشو|br|Oadvezh Taishō|ca|Període Taishō|cs|Období Taišó|de|Taishō-Zeit|eo|Taiŝo-epoko|es|Era Taishō|et|Taishō ajastu|eu|Taishō aroa|fa|دوره تایشو|fi|Taishō-kausi|fr|Ère Taishō|he|תקופת טאישו|hi|ताइशो युग|hu|Taisó-kor|hy|Տայսյո|id|Zaman Taishō|it|Periodo Taishō|ja|大正|ko|다이쇼 시대|lt|Taišio laikotarpis|lv|Taišo periods|ml|തായ്ഷോ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Taishō|nl|Taishoperiode|no|Taishō-perioden|pl|Taishō (okres)|pt|Período Taishō|ro|Perioada Taishō|ru|Тайсё|sh|Taishō period|simple|Taishō era|sr|Таишо период|sv|Taishō|th|ยุคไทโช|tl|Panahong Taishō|tr|Taişo Dönemi|uk|Період Тайсьо|uz|Taishō davri|vi|Thời kỳ Đại Chính|zh|大正|zh_classical|大正 (年號)|zh_min_nan|Tāi-chèng|zh_yue|大正 (日本年號)|qid=Q329174}} 13) promoted to a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}} and renamed its current name, “Oiso Shrine”<ref name="神社庁"> [http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=653 Oiso Shrine] (Shiga Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref>.

During the {{ill|1983 South American Rugby Championship|Q1135329|qid=Q1135329}}, parts of the precincts were taken for the {{ill|Japan National Route 8|Q640239|qid=Q640239}} bypass and the {{ill|Tokaido Shinkansen|Q660895|qid=Q660895}}, resulting in the precincts being divided.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Oiso-jinja, honden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Main hall (right, a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}})<br>Suwa Shrine (left, a cultural property designated by Ōmihachiman City)}}]]
[[File:Oiso-jinja, sandou.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Approach and shrine grove (Oisonomori)}}]]
* Main hall ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}) – Rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1581|Q6717|qid=Q6717}}). It is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} structure with a one-bay front porch and a cypress-bark roof. It features splendid decorations such as openwork arabesque carvings on the {{ill|kaerumata|Q123117911|qid=Q123117911}}, carvings on the {{ill|tabasami|Q124660898|qid=Q124660898}}, and latticework panels around the lower walls of the core. According to the {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}}, it was constructed by Shibata Iehisa, and a connection has been suggested with policies related to the formation of the castle town of {{ill|Azuchi Castle|Q786888|qid=Q786888}} under {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}<ref name="国指定 奥石神社本殿"/><ref>Explanation board for the Oiso Shrine main hall within the precincts.</ref>.
* Middle gate
* Worship hall
* Kagura hall
* Shrine office

=== Oisonomori ===
A nationally designated {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}}. The shrine grove surrounding the buildings is called “Oisonomori.” The present forest consists mainly of {{ill|Cryptomeria|Q147388|qid=Q147388}}, {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|Q917187|qid=Q917187}}, and {{ill|Pine|Q12024|qid=Q12024}}. According to tradition in the *Oiso Shrine Honki*, the land was once split open with water welling up and was uninhabitable, but when Ishibe no Ōmuraji planted saplings and prayed to the gods, it became a great forest; Ishibe no Ōmuraji lived to over a hundred years, and thus it came to be called the “Oiso (Old and Revived) Forest.” The name appears in a poem from the first year of {{ill|Manju (era)|de|Manju (Ära)|fa|مانجو (دوره)|fr|Ère Manju|ia|Manju (era)|id|Manju|ja|万寿|ko|만주 (연호)|ru|Мандзю (нэнго)|simple|Manju (era)|sr|Манџу (ера)|tr|Manju (dönem)|zh|萬壽|zh_yue|萬壽|qid=Q1194155}} ({{ill|1024|Q19265|qid=Q19265}}) in the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}}, and it is also introduced as a {{ill|Utamakura|Q1588579|qid=Q1588579}} of Ōmi Province in works such as the *{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}*, *Nōin Utamakura*, and *Waka Shogakushō*. Because it lay along the medieval {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306}} and the early modern Nakasendō, it is also mentioned in travelogues from the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} onward, such as the *{{ill|Tōkan Kikō|Q11528660|qid=Q11528660}}*. For these reasons, as a place of long-standing and valuable history, the forest area has been designated a National Historic Site{{Sfn|Oisonomori (Heibonsha)|1991}}<ref name="国指定 老蘇森"/><ref>Explanation board for Oisonomori within the precincts.</ref>.

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
* Suwa Shrine (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Ōmihachiman City)
*: Enshrined deities: {{ill|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata|Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Yasakatome|Q9150392|qid=Q9150392|lt=Yasakatome-no-Mikoto}}. Located to the west of the main hall. Although the exact construction date is unknown, it is thought to have been built around the Azuchi–Momoyama period. It is a one-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} structure with a cypress-bark roof. Repairs were carried out in the 7th year of {{ill|Ansei|Q1327259|qid=Q1327259}} ({{ill|1860|Q7691|qid=Q7691}}) and in {{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}} (Meiji 13), and it is regarded as a building that retains much of its original materials in good condition<ref>Explanation board for the Suwa Shrine main hall within the Oiso Shrine precincts.</ref>.
* Yoshizumi Inari Shrine

File:Oiso-jinja, Yoshizumi-Inarisha.jpg|Yoshizumi Inari Shrine
</gallery>

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Main hall (structure) – Built in the Azuchi–Momoyama period, Tenshō 9 ({{ill|1581|Q6717|qid=Q6717}}). Designated on April 17, {{ill|1902|Q2043|qid=Q2043}} (Meiji 35)<ref name="国指定 奥石神社本殿">{{National Cultural Properties Database|102|1474|Oiso Shrine Main Hall}}</ref>.
